slides.kicker: The Intent Signal Playbook, in 9 slides
slides.title: You don't have a lead problem. You have a timing problem.
slides.sub: How revenue teams find the 40 accounts worth calling this week, out of thousands that technically fit.

slides.title: 412 accounts in the view. No idea which 40 matter.
slides.body: It is 8:40 on a Tuesday. The list is sorted by company name. Nothing in it says who hired a VP of Sales three weeks ago, or who had four people reading about the category last Thursday.

visual.label: Buying more contacts adds rows to the same undifferentiated pile.

slides.title: One signal is close to worthless.

rungs.name: Weak
rungs.note: Someone read your blog. One signal, one family.

rungs.name: Better
rungs.note: They came back for the product page. Two signals, still one family.

rungs.name: Strong
rungs.note: Category research off-site, product page on-site, a competitor searched. Two families.

rungs.name: Very strong
rungs.note: Four-plus signals from three families that could not have caused each other.

slides.after: Strength comes from independence, not volume.

slides.title: Six dimensions, scored in ninety seconds.

head: Dimension
Weight
What it answers
rows: Do they look like a company that buys this?
What do they appear to be researching?
Are they interacting with us specifically?

slides.after: Score each 0 to 5, apply the weights, and the list sorts itself out of 100. Fit is heaviest because it is the only dimension that does not decay.

slides.title: A six-week-old signal describes a moment that has passed.

head: Days since newest signal
Score
rows: 5. Whatever prompted it is still an open topic
3. Act only if another dimension carries weight

slides.title: Three tiers and one exit ramp.

items.name: Tier 1. Contact now
items.what: Personalised outreach same day. One written hypothesis. 15 to 25 accounts per SDR per week, no more.

items.name: Tier 2. Research and monitor
items.what: Named owner, weekly review, one thing to watch for. Promote the moment a second signal family fires.

items.name: Tier 3. Nurture
items.what: Marketing's, not an SDR's. Be present and credible when the trigger eventually happens.

items.name: Disqualify
items.what: Remove it and record why. High intent never overrides poor fit.

slides.title: Five minutes, five questions, one written hypothesis.

items.text: **Fit.** Name the closest existing customer and the use case.
**Intent.** What problem appears to be in play, in the buyer's language?
**Recency.** When, and is it a cluster or a single point?
**Trigger.** What changed in the last 90 days that you are allowed to reference?
**Buyer.** Who owns this problem? A person, not a title.

slides.after: Output: "Because [observable change], and given [area of interest], [role] may be working on [specific problem]."

slides.title: Use intent to pick the account. Never to write the message.

items.text: "Hey Dana, I noticed your company has been researching sales engagement software. Do you have 15 minutes Thursday?"

"Dana, you've added nine SDRs since July. Teams usually start looking at how outbound is managed when hiring outpaces the managers who can coach it. Is that the shape of the problem on your side, or something else?"

slides.after: The test: would the sentence still make sense if the signal data had never existed?

slides.title: 100 accounts down to 5, in one week.

rows.label: Target accounts in the quarter's list
Meaningful intent in the last 60 days
Two or more signal families agree

slides.after: Two SDRs, five accounts, three contacts each, a four-day week. A smaller number than most teams are comfortable with, and that is the point.
